criteria: workdays.py defines two functions, add_workdays(start, days, holidays=()) returning a date and count_workdays(first, last, holidays=()) returning an int, where dates are datetime.date objects, a working day is a day from Monday to Friday that is not in holidays, and holidays is any collection of dates that defaults to none.

add_workdays with days > 0 returns the days-th working day after start; start itself is never counted, whether it is a working day or not; from Friday 6 Nov 2026, one working day later is Monday 9 Nov 2026.
add_workdays with days < 0 returns the -days-th working day before start, by the same rule in the other direction (start itself is never counted, whether it is a working day or not).
add_workdays with days == 0 returns start when start is a working day, and otherwise returns the first working day after start.
add_workdays requires days to be an int; a bool or any other type for days raises TypeError.
count_workdays(first, last, holidays) counts the working days from first to last, both included.
count_workdays, when first is after last, returns the negative of count_workdays(last, first, holidays).
In both add_workdays and count_workdays, a holiday that falls on a weekend changes nothing.
Neither add_workdays nor count_workdays changes the holidays collection passed to it.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
